classification.difficultyReason: The same rhombus-diagonal-plus-Pythagoras idea as p34-q12, but the parts supply the plan: right angle, then halves, then hypotenuse. The student recalls the diagonal properties and applies Pythagoras to given legs. There is no need to see that a half-diagonal is missing, so it is easier than the unscaffolded reverse problem.

content.prompt: The diagonals of rhombus $ABCD$ meet at $E$.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so $\angle AEB=90^\circ$.

The diagonals bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}AE&=30\div2=15\text{ cm}\\BE&=16\div2=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

$\triangle AEB$ is right-angled at $E$ and $AB$ is its hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=15^2+8^2\\AB^2&=225+64\\AB^2&=289\\AB&=17\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

answer.short: a) $90^\circ$; b) $AE=15\text{ cm}$, $BE=8\text{ cm}$; c) $17\text{ cm}$
